name: IA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Republican McGowan's large fundraising edge over Democrat Dawson
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The seat's R+15 lean and the absence of any Democratic polling or rating support make this a Republican stronghold even with Feenstra retiring. McGowan's fundraising advantage and markets pricing a Republican win near 95% reinforce a Safe R call.
model.watch: A contested Republican primary producing a damaged nominee, or a late Democratic money infusion, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Iowa's 4th District is a strongly Republican seat, and Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves an open race rather than a competitive one. Republican Chris McGowan has raised nearly $680,000 with outside support, while Democrat David Dawson has raised about $136,000 with little cash on hand and no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's R+15 lean and the lopsided resource gap. Prediction markets put the Democratic win chance at roughly 4%. The seat remains safely Republican, with the primary outcome the main open question.
